Inspected the actual current Definition body: Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. When $\sigma$=0, the preimage of E is all of R if m belongs to E and empty otherwise, so $N(m,0)=\delta_m$ in [[def-dirac-measure]].

Inspected the actual current Statement body: Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

Inspected the actual current Definition body: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $X$ and $Y$ be real Hilbert spaces and let $K:X\to Y$ be a compact linear operator of infinite rank, viewed as an inverse model with exact datum $Kx$. Here compact means that the image of every bounded subset has compact closure. Write $N(K)=\{x\in X:Kx=0\}$ and $H_0=\overline{\operatorname{ran}K}$. Fix a positive singular system $(s_j,v_j,u_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ for $K$, where $\mathbb N=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$, $s_1\ge s_2\ge\cdots>0$, $s_j\to0$, $Kv_j=s_ju_j$, $(v_j)$ is a complete orthonormal basis of $N(K)^\perp$, and $(u_j)$ is a complete orthonormal basis of $H_0$. A complete orthonormal basis is an orthonormal family whose closed linear span is the whole indicated subspace. These are the compact SVD conventions; in particular, this model concerns minimum-norm representatives in $N(K)^\perp$ and does not estimate a kernel component.

Inspected the actual current Definition body: Let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$
([[def-finite-probability-vector]]). They define finite probability spaces
with outcome weights $p_x$ and $q_x$, respectively
([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). For $h:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$, write
$E_Ph:=\sum_xp_xh(x)$ and $E_Qh:=\sum_xq_xh(x)$; these are the finite
expectations ([[def-expectation-on-a-finite-probability-space]]). Test the
simple null $H_0:P$ against the simple alternative $H_1:Q$. A randomized test is a function
$\phi:\mathcal X\to[0,1]$, where $\phi(x)$ is the probability of rejecting
$H_0$ after observing $x$; thus $1-\phi(x)$ is the probability of accepting
$H_0$ ([[def-randomized-test]]). Its type-I error is
$\sum_xp_x\phi(x)$, and its type-II error is
$\sum_xq_x(1-\phi(x))$ ([[def-test-size-and-power]]).

Inspected the actual current Definition body: Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, where separable means having a countable dense subset, and let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space. A real isonormal Gaussian process on $H$ is a family $Z(g)$ of real random variables with finite second moments, indexed by $g\in H$, such that $g\mapsto[Z(g)]$ is linear into $L^2(\mathbb P)$, $\mathbb E Z(g)=0$, and $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(h)]=\langle g,h\rangle_H$. It is also required that for every finite orthonormal tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_m)$ the variables $Z(e_1),\ldots,Z(e_m)$ are independent and each has density $\varphi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/2}$. For any finite list of vectors, expressing them in an orthonormal basis of their finite-dimensional span shows that their process values have the corresponding linear-image Gaussian law. Here $L^2(\mathbb P)$ identifies square-integrable random variables that agree almost surely. When $H\ne\{0\}$, all unit-vector marginals have the same law; write $N(a,\sigma^2)$ for the law of $a+\sigma Z(e)$ for any unit vector $e\in H$ and $\sigma\ge0$.

Inspected the actual current Statement body: Let $(X_n)$ and $(Y_n)$ be real random variables on one probability space, and let $X$ be a real random variable (possibly on another space). If $X_n\Rightarrow X$ and $Y_n\to c$ in probability for $c\in\mathbb R$, then $X_n+Y_n\Rightarrow X+c$ and $X_nY_n\Rightarrow cX$. If $c\ne0$, define $Q_n=X_n/Y_n$ on $\{Y_n\ne0\}$ and give $Q_n$ any fixed value on $\{Y_n=0\}$. Then $Q_n\Rightarrow X/c$.
